page: Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor featuring 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs built on x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 128 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU thread. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, FMA, and CLWB, while excluding AVX-512 extensions. Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the instance provides baseline network performance of 25 Gbps without bundled local instance storage or attached GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show high multi-threaded compute performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core execution, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation via Clang. PassMark testing demonstrates upper-quartile scores across general CPU processing, instruction execution, physics calculations, hardware encryption, and database operations. In key-value memory benchmark testing, it achieves 67.6 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks reaches 4432.18 GB/sec in the top quartile, while uncached 256 MB memory read and write throughput average 122.58 GB/sec and 60.35 GB/sec respectively.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM memory density offers an efficient hardware profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive RAM per core or local NVMe storage. Multi-threaded processing capacity and 25 Gbps network performance make this instance suitable for batch processing, software compilation systems, high-concurrency web application backends, in-memory key-value caching, and lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by a dedicated 32-core, 64-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Managed by the AWS Nitro System, it provides 128 GB of 3 GHz DDR4 RAM with a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, alongside a 25 Gbps network interface and zero local storage. Benchmarks place its multi-core CPU capacity in the top 25%, excelling in stress-ng tests, PassMark encryption, Redis SET operations reaching 67.6 million per second, and Clang software compilation. Cached small-block memory reads achieve top-quartile speeds, though uncached large-block transfers remain average. Without bundled local disk space or GPU hardware, this instance yields high resource density and processing efficiency for compute-heavy applications. It is suited for software build pipelines, batch processing jobs, web serving, in-memory caching, and CPU-based data transformations.
